title: SQL Injection - Login Bypass
impact: An attacker can bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the administrator account without knowing the legitimate password.
remediation: Use prepared statements and parameterized SQL queries to prevent malicious input from altering SQL commands.

title: SQL Injection - User Credential Extraction
impact: An attacker can retrieve user credentials, including email addresses and password hashes, through the product search endpoint.
remediation: Use parameterized queries and avoid concatenating user input into SQL statements. Apply least-privilege database access and secure password storage.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via Product Search
impact: An attacker can execute JavaScript in a victim's browser through a crafted search query, potentially enabling phishing or unauthorized actions within the victim's session.
remediation: Encode and sanitize user input, apply context-aware output encoding, and implement a restrictive Content Security Policy.

title: DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting
impact: An attacker can execute malicious JavaScript in a victim's browser by manipulating the search input processed by the DOM. This could lead to phishing, session compromise, or unauthorized actions performed through the victim's browser.
remediation: Validate and sanitize untrusted input, use safe DOM manipulation methods such as textContent instead of innerHTML, apply context-aware output encoding, and implement a restrictive Content Security Policy.
